paper.title: IDPrior: Decoupling Identity Generation from Facial Image Synthesis
paper.summary: Large-scale identity-labeled face datasets are essential for training modern face recognition models, yet collecting and annotating such data is costly and raises privacy and ethical concerns. Existing synthetic face generation methods typically derive identities from predefined class labels, unconditional image generation, or predefined latent sampling strategies, without explicitly modeling the underlying distribution of facial identities. In this paper, we propose IDPrior, a two-stage framework that decouples identity generation from image synthesis. We first learn a diffusion prior in the embedding space of a pretrained face recognition model to model the distribution of facial identities and generate novel identity embeddings. These embeddings are then used to condition a pretrained identity-conditioned diffusion model (DM), enabling the synthesis of multiple images of the same identity. This modular design provides a scalable approach to identity generation while remaining compatible with existing and future identity-conditioned DMs. Experiments indicate that IDPrior generates diverse and well-separated identities while maintaining a closer correspondence to the distribution of authentic identities. Face recognition models trained on datasets generated using IDPrior-generated identities achieve competitive or improved performance compared with existing synthetic-data-based methods across multiple face verification benchmarks. Code and generated datasets are publicly available at https://github.com/fdbtrs/IDperturb.

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the high cost, privacy concerns, and lack of explicit identity distribution modeling in existing synthetic face generation methods used for training face recognition models.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Data scarcity and annotation cost for high-quality, diverse identity-labeled facial datasets.
analysis.executive_summary: IDPrior decouples identity generation from image synthesis by learning a diffusion prior in the embedding space of a pretrained face recognition model. This approach generates novel, well-separated identity embeddings that are more representative of authentic identity distributions than existing methods, enabling scalable and privacy-preserving data augmentation for face recognition tasks.

technical_breakdown.architecture: 1. Diffusion prior in face embedding space for identity generation. 2. Pretrained identity-conditioned diffusion model (DM) for image synthesis.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Uses a pretrained face recognition model's embedding space to model the distribution of facial identities. Generates multiple images per identity by conditioning the diffusion model on the generated embeddings.

paper.title: MV-Sign: Multi-View 3D Motion Integration and Enhanced Text-to-Motion Conditioning for Sign Language Production
paper.summary: Sign language production (SLP) aims to generate appropriate sign language motion from spoken language text. However, current 3D SLP methods suffer from noisy supervision and weak text conditioning. Specifically, these methods typically rely on pseudo-3D motion data fitted from single-view frontal videos, which introduces severe self-occlusion and loses fine-grained hand details, ultimately degrading downstream production. To overcome these limitations, we propose a comprehensive framework that jointly integrates multi-view 3D motion data and optimizes the text-conditioning pathway. First, we introduce How2Sign-MV3D, a high-fidelity dataset constructed via a novel cross-view curation pipeline that fuses multi-view estimates to resolve occlusions and filter non-signing segments. Second, we design a robust SLP model incorporating a sign-aware spatio-temporal VQ-VAE (ST-VQVAE) for joint body-hand tokenization, a pseudo-gloss adapter, and keyframe-aware retrieval to enhance text-to-motion alignment. Evaluated on the How2Sign benchmark, our framework reduces body and hand DTW-PA-JPE by 32.8% and 20.9% respectively compared to the state-of-the-art. Finally, we release two new high-quality 3D datasets, ASLCitizen-3D and MM-WAuslan-MV3D, alongside SGNify-MV as a multi-view video benchmark to support broader community research.

By combining high-fidelity multi-view datasets with a sign-aware spatio-temporal VQ-VAE and keyframe-aware retrieval, it significantly improves the accuracy and fidelity of generated sign language motions.

paper.title: Rain Beyond Streaks: Cascaded Realistic Rain and Wet Surface Synthesis via Scene Priors
paper.summary: Realistic rain synthesis is a persistent challenge for vision systems operating in adverse weather. Existing methods primarily focus on generating rain streaks, often neglecting consequent surface effects such as reflections and puddles, which are critical for perceptual realism and robustness of downstream vision tasks. We introduce CascadeRS, a rain synthesis framework that leverages depth and segmentation priors to render scene-consistent rain and surface effects. In addition to rain streaks, CascadeRS produces reflections and puddles aligned with scene semantics through a physics-inspired zero-shot, controllable generative pipeline. It produces photorealistic rainy urban scenes, with high perceptual realism, which we validate qualitatively with an extensive user study and quantitatively. We produce the Cityscapes-CascadeRS dataset, to study downstream task performance under real rainy conditions. Our results establish CascadeRS as a scalable and realistic rain-generation framework for evaluating and enhancing the robustness of vision in adverse rainy weather. Code and dataset are available via https://github.com/nis-research/CascadeRainSynthesis

analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the gap in realistic adverse weather simulation by introducing a framework that synthesizes not just rain streaks, but also semantically aligned surface effects. By leveraging scene priors, it enables the creation of high-fidelity rainy urban scenes, which is crucial for improving the robustness of autonomous driving and other vision systems operating in real-world rainy conditions.

paper.title: GEKey: Learning Geodesic Eccentric 3D Keypoints via Self-Supervision
paper.summary: Point clouds represent 3D object geometry as sets of spatial coordinates. A fundamental task in their analysis is keypoint detection, i.e., identifying a sparse subset of points that captures the most salient features. While supervised methods rely on manual annotations, unsupervised approaches leverage intrinsic geometric properties to localize keypoints without human input. We introduce GEKey, a self-supervised framework that uses the geodesic eccentricity transform, an SE(3)-invariant geometric measure, to identify instance-specific salient points. These points serve as pseudo-labels to train a model that aligns its predictions with the object's intrinsic structure. GEKey is simple, efficient, and robust, preserving intra-class variation by balancing instance-specific and category-level structure. Extensive experiments on ShapeNetCoreV2, KeypointNet, CAPE, ITOP, and DeformingThings4D show state-of-the-art performance in both keypoint detection and alignment, with strong resilience to noise, downsampling, deformations, and real-world conditions. The code and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/Pierreoo/GEKey.

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the challenge of detecting salient 3D keypoints on point clouds without relying on expensive manual annotations or rigid category-level templates that fail to capture instance-specific geometric variations.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Data annotation dependency and the lack of instance-specific adaptability in unsupervised keypoint detection methods.
analysis.executive_summary: GEKey introduces a self-supervised framework that leverages the geodesic eccentricity transform, an SE(3)-invariant metric, to generate pseudo-labels for keypoint detection. This approach eliminates the need for manual annotations while preserving intra-class variation, offering a robust and efficient solution for 3D object analysis in noisy and deformed real-world conditions.

key_metrics.primary_metric: State-of-the-art performance in keypoint detection and alignment across multiple benchmarks.
key_metrics.baseline: Supervised methods and existing unsupervised approaches on ShapeNetCoreV2, KeypointNet, CAPE, ITOP, and DeformingThings4D.

technical_breakdown.method: The framework uses the geodesic eccentricity transform to identify instance-specific salient points, which serve as pseudo-labels to train a model that aligns predictions with the object's intrinsic structure.
technical_breakdown.architecture: A self-supervised learning pipeline that integrates geometric feature extraction (geodesic eccentricity) with a keypoint detection model trained via pseudo-label alignment.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Utilizes SE(3)-invariant geometric measures to ensure robustness to rotation and translation; balances instance-specific and category-level structure to maintain intra-class variation.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Described as simple and efficient, with strong resilience to noise, downsampling, and deformations; specific computational complexity or training time figures are not provided in the summary.

paper.title: Guidance Is a Field, Not a Scalar: Interval-Integrated Classifier-Free Guidance for One-Step Video Generation
paper.summary: One-step generators built on MeanFlow synthesize a video in a single function evaluation, yet inherit a rigid treatment of classifier-free guidance (CFG): the guidance scale is frozen during training or, at best, exposed as a single scalar. This conflicts with mounting evidence that the optimal guidance is not a constant but a field that varies with the noise level, with spatial content, and, for video, with frame position. Every existing remedy presupposes a multi-step sampler along which guidance can be re-scheduled--an assumption one-step models violate by construction. We resolve this tension through a single observation: because the MeanFlow target is an integral over a noise interval, an arbitrary guidance field can be absorbed into the target itself and compiled into one evaluation. We formalize this as the interval-integrated CFG identity, prove that the compiled guidance carries no schedule-discretization error and can thus match or exceed any finite multi-step sampler, and instantiate it as AGAVE, which equips the average-velocity field with a learnable temporal schedule, a free motion-saliency spatial modulation, and a frame-position asymmetry. Adding fewer than ten scalars at zero inference cost, AGAVE surpasses all one-step baselines on VBench, UCF-101 and MSR-VTT while matching multi-step guided sampling. Project repository: https://github.com/YMlinfeng/AGAVE.

analysis.problem_statement: One-step video generators based on MeanFlow cannot effectively utilize dynamic, spatially or temporally varying classifier-free guidance (CFG) schedules because they lack the multi-step sampling trajectory required to re-schedule guidance at different noise levels.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Inefficiency and rigidity of guidance mechanisms in one-step diffusion models, specifically the inability to apply non-constant, content-aware guidance without multi-step sampling overhead.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper resolves the conflict between the rigid scalar guidance of one-step MeanFlow models and the evidence that optimal guidance is a dynamic field. By formalizing an 'interval-integrated CFG identity,' it allows arbitrary guidance fields to be compiled into a single function evaluation, eliminating schedule-discretization error. This enables one-step video generation to match or exceed the quality of multi-step guided sampling at zero additional inference cost.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Performance on VBench, UCF-101, and MSR-VTT benchmarks
key_metrics.metric_value: Surpasses all one-step baselines and matches multi-step guided sampling
key_metrics.baseline: One-step MeanFlow baselines and multi-step guided samplers

technical_breakdown.method: The method leverages the fact that the MeanFlow target is an integral over a noise interval, allowing an arbitrary guidance field to be absorbed into the target itself. This is formalized as the interval-integrated CFG identity, which compiles the guidance into a single evaluation without discretization error.
technical_breakdown.architecture: AGAVE (Average-velocity field with learnable guidance), which equips the average-velocity field with a learnable temporal schedule, free motion-saliency spatial modulation, and frame-position asymmetry.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Adds fewer than ten learnable scalar parameters to the model. Uses a learnable temporal schedule, motion-saliency spatial modulation, and frame-position asymmetry to define the guidance field.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Zero additional inference cost compared to standard one-step evaluation; minimal training overhead due to fewer than ten added parameters.

paper.title: Coverage Hides Churn: Auditing and Preserving Conformal Decisions as VLM Label Registries Grow
paper.summary: Vision-language classifiers can learn new labels from text alone, so the label lists they serve keep growing. We show that this growth silently changes conformal decisions about old labels. Common softmax-based conformal scores compare each label with an average over all labels; adding labels changes that average, and with it the score of every old label, even when the model, the image, and the old calibration data stay the same. Recalibrating after the update keeps the coverage guarantee, yet across eleven settings it changes at least one old decision on 53-90% of new images. Coverage cannot reveal this, because it checks only the true label: in five controlled settings that keep the old calibration, so that only the normalizer changes, old-class coverage moves by at most 0.01 while 60-67% of images change. We propose a lifecycle audit that measures these changes alongside coverage and set size, and a simple fix, PrefixCP: each class keeps the label registry that existed when it was added. Its old decisions then never change, each class keeps exact class-conditional coverage under exchangeability, and one prefix scan computes all historical normalizers at once. PrefixCP recovers 40.9-58.5% of the set-size gap between never updating the reference and recalibrating, which gives smaller sets but changes old decisions.
paper.comment: Accepted at WACV 2027. Includes supplementary material

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the issue where adding new labels to Vision-Language Model (VLM) registries silently alters conformal prediction decisions for existing labels due to changes in the softmax normalizer, a phenomenon that standard coverage metrics fail to detect.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Reliability and consistency of uncertainty quantification in dynamic, open-world classification systems.
analysis.executive_summary: As VLMs expand their label spaces, standard conformal prediction methods suffer from 'decision churn,' where the addition of new classes changes the predicted confidence and acceptance/rejection status of old classes despite no change in model weights or input data. This undermines the stability of automated decision-making pipelines. The paper introduces a lifecycle audit and a prefix-based calibration method to preserve historical decision consistency while maintaining coverage guarantees.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Recovery of set-size gap between static reference and recalibrated dynamic settings
key_metrics.baseline: Recalibrating after label update (which preserves coverage but changes 53-90% of old decisions)

technical_breakdown.method: The authors propose PrefixCP, a method where each class retains the label registry snapshot from the time of its addition. This ensures that the normalizer used for conformal scoring remains consistent with the historical context of that class, preventing decision churn for old labels.
technical_breakdown.architecture: A lifecycle audit framework that tracks decision changes alongside coverage and set size, coupled with a prefix-based calibration mechanism that maintains historical normalizers for each class.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Uses a single prefix scan to compute all historical normalizers simultaneously. The method relies on exchangeability assumptions to maintain exact class-conditional coverage for each class within its respective prefix context.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: The solution involves a single prefix scan for normalizer computation, implying linear complexity relative to the number of labels in the registry, which is computationally efficient compared to full recalibration.

paper.title: PSGAgent: Enhancing MLLMs' Dynamic Visual Perception for Panoptic Scene Graph Generation via Agentic Reasoning
paper.summary: Panoptic Scene Graph generation (PSG) requires holistic yet fine-grained reasoning over complex relations among objects. However, current Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) applied to PSG suffer from a perception bottleneck: they function as static observers limited by fixed-resolution views. As a result, models often overlook critical relations involving small or peripheral objects and struggle to differentiate ambiguous predicates in complex scenes. To address these limitations, we propose PSGAgent, an agentic framework that enhances visual perception for PSG through a think-act-observe loop. PSGAgent allows MLLMs to dynamically refine their visual perception using two tools: a Region Zoom-In Tool for local exploration of small or boundary relations and a Visual Highlight Tool for relation-focused segmentation that filters out irrelevant contextual noise. To optimize decision-making, we construct a two-stage training pipeline. First, we create a high-quality, error-aware Multimodal Chain-of-Thought (M-CoT) dataset that provides robust supervision for cold-start learning. Then, we design a novel hierarchical reward mechanism integrated with Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) to enable strategic and adaptive tool usage. Extensive experiments on the PSG benchmark show that PSGAgent achieves SOTA performance, demonstrating strong capability in both holistic and fine-grained scene understanding.

analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the limitation of MLLMs as static observers by introducing an agentic framework that enables dynamic visual refinement. By allowing models to actively zoom in and highlight specific regions, it significantly improves the accuracy of scene graph generation in complex environments.

paper.title: OptST: Optimizing Semantic Tokenization for LLM-Enhanced Recommendation
paper.summary: Semantic information can enrich the identifiers and structured fields used by recommender systems. Semantic tokenization provides a structured representation of this information by converting LLM-derived user profiles into discrete tokens. In the common two-stage pipeline, the tokenizer is trained before the recommender. Its token assignments are then treated as fixed input features during recommendation training. As a result, the downstream recommender can learn how to use the assigned indices, but it cannot revise the semantic partition that produced them. Making this partition task-aware is difficult because nearest-code assignment is discrete, and unconstrained adaptation may also distort the geometry learned during pretraining. Moreover, a fixed token depth exposes the same semantic resolution to every interaction. We thus propose OptST (Optimizing Semantic Tokenization), which makes a pretrained tokenizer responsive to downstream recommendation. To revise token assignments without directly updating the pretrained encoder or base codebooks, OptST learns a low-rank deformation whose drift is limited by an anchor regularizer. Recommendation supervision reaches this transformation through a straight-through estimator, while prediction retains hard nearest-code assignments. Beyond adapting the assignments themselves, OptST selects an interaction-conditioned prefix to control how much residual detail is exposed to the recommender. Experiments on four public datasets show that OptST achieves the highest AUC among conventional and LLM-enhanced baselines. Its improvements also persist across different recommendation backbones. These results establish task-aware semantic tokenization as an effective interface between LLM-derived profiles and downstream recommendation models.

analysis.problem_statement: The paper addresses the limitation of fixed, task-agnostic semantic tokenization in LLM-enhanced recommendation systems, where discrete token assignments cannot be revised by the downstream recommender to optimize for specific recommendation tasks.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: The disconnect between static LLM-derived semantic representations and the dynamic, task-specific requirements of downstream recommendation models, specifically the inability to adapt discrete code assignments without distorting pre-trained geometric structures.
analysis.executive_summary: This work bridges the gap between LLM profile generation and recommendation by introducing a task-aware adaptation layer for semantic tokenization. By allowing the recommender to influence token assignments via a low-rank deformation, it improves the alignment between semantic features and prediction objectives without retraining the base LLM encoder.

key_metrics.primary_metric: AUC (Area Under the Curve)
key_metrics.baseline: Conventional and LLM-enhanced recommendation baselines

technical_breakdown.method: OptST learns a low-rank deformation of the semantic tokenizer that is responsive to downstream recommendation supervision. It uses a straight-through estimator to allow gradients to flow from the recommendation loss to the token assignment transformation, while retaining hard nearest-code assignments for the final prediction.
technical_breakdown.architecture: The system consists of a pre-trained semantic tokenizer (encoder and codebooks), a low-rank deformation module with an anchor regularizer to limit drift, and a downstream recommendation backbone that consumes the adapted tokens. It also includes a mechanism to select an interaction-conditioned prefix to control semantic resolution.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Key techniques include low-rank matrix deformation for parameter efficiency, an anchor regularizer to preserve pre-training geometry, and the straight-through estimator (STE) to handle the non-differentiable nature of nearest-code assignment during training.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: The method adds a low-rank adaptation layer, implying minimal additional computational overhead compared to full fine-tuning of the tokenizer. The use of STE allows for efficient backpropagation through discrete operations.

paper.title: The Last Mile to the Real World: Agent-Native Primitives as Reusable Building Blocks for Solving Real-World Tasks
paper.summary: How can an agent handle a real-world task end to end? Frontier models with their own harnesses still fall short on real-world benchmarks: on Terminal-Bench 4.0, GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex resolves 37.3% of the tasks and Claude Opus 5 with Claude Code 51.8%. These tasks fail at the step from reaching a resource to applying it, which we call the last mile to the real world. Existing approaches put the resource within reach but leave the competence to apply it with the caller, so each harness rebuilds that competence. We introduce agent-native primitives, reusable units that equip a resource with a resident LLM that applies it in context and communicates with other primitives, and HEELO (Harness Engineering around Evolving Agent-Native Primitives for the Last Mile to Real-WOrld Tasks), a harness engineering framework that builds each task's harness from a library of such primitives. HEELO composes the primitives a task needs into a task-specific graph, verifies the result against evidence from the environment, revises the primitives a failure implicates, and admits new or improved primitives after validation. We instantiate HEELO with eight primitive families, each built for one kind of task, and evaluate them on more than twenty benchmarks. Dev-Primitives raise Terminal-Bench 4.0 resolution from 37.3% under Codex to 55.5% on the same backbone, Harness Primitives composed per task raise Terminal-Bench 2.0 Pass@1 from 60.0% for the seed harness to 72.2%, Tool Primitives raise ToolBench pass rate from 55.8% to 75.1%, and Navigation Primitives raise GAIA-Text-103 accuracy from 45.6% to 58.3%. On the 46 real-world tasks of our heelo.dev platform, Claude Opus 5.5 with Claude Code and GPT-6.1 Sol with Codex complete 9 each on their own and 39 and 35 when connected to HEELO through our MCP server, with 1.9$\times$ and 2.3$\times$ less time and 1.55$\times$ lower cost per completed task.

analysis.problem_statement: Frontier AI agents fail to complete real-world tasks because existing frameworks provide access to resources but do not encapsulate the specific competence required to apply those resources in context, creating a 'last mile' gap between resource retrieval and task execution.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: The lack of reusable, context-aware execution competence in agent harnesses, which forces each new task or harness to rebuild the logic for applying retrieved resources rather than leveraging resident, specialized capabilities.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper introduces 'agent-native primitives,' reusable units that combine resources with resident LLMs to handle specific task types, addressing the fragmentation of agent capabilities. By proposing HEELO, a framework that dynamically composes these primitives into task-specific graphs and iteratively refines them based on environmental feedback, it significantly improves end-to-end task resolution rates across diverse benchmarks without requiring new foundation model training.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Terminal-Bench 4.0 task resolution rate
key_metrics.baseline: 37.3% (GPT-5.6 Sol with Codex)

technical_breakdown.method: HEELO (Harness Engineering around Evolving Agent-Native Primitives for the Last Mile to Real-WOrld Tasks) constructs a task-specific graph by composing a library of agent-native primitives. It verifies results against environmental evidence, identifies failures, and revises or admits new primitives to the library after validation.
technical_breakdown.architecture: The system consists of agent-native primitives (reusable units with resident LLMs for specific resource application), a harness engineering framework that builds task-specific graphs, and an MCP server interface for connecting frontier models (e.g., Claude Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol) to the HEELO infrastructure.
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Eight distinct primitive families are instantiated for different task types (e.g., Dev, Harness, Tool, Navigation). The framework employs a verification loop that uses environment evidence to validate outputs and triggers primitive revision or admission based on failure analysis.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: The approach reduces per-task cost and time (1.55x lower cost, 1.9-2.3x less time) by reusing validated primitives rather than rebuilding competence from scratch for each task, though the initial construction of the primitive library and graph composition adds architectural overhead.

paper.title: Reviving the Discarded High-Resolution Feature for Transformer-Based Tiny Object Detection
paper.summary: Tiny object detection remains challenging because tiny instances occupy only a few pixels, and their fine-grained details are easily lost during feature downsampling. Although the highest-resolution feature preserves rich local details for tiny objects, DETR-like detectors often discard it due to its large computational cost, while directly reintroducing this feature also brings dense background noise. To address this problem, we propose ReDHF, a novel framework that Revives the Discarded High-resolution Feature for tiny object detection. ReDHF has three cooperative components. Cross-Scale Deformable Fusion (CSDF) first constructs a semantically enhanced highest-resolution feature and injects its fine-grained details into the shallow feature under a moderate cost. Ellipse-Guided Shallow Supervision (EGSS) then guides the enhanced feature to learn more reliable classification and localization priors by applying geometry-adaptive auxiliary supervision. Full-Scale Query Interaction (FSQI) further enables decoder queries to access both low-level details and high-level semantic information, allowing them to aggregate richer cues for tiny objects. Extensive experiments show that ReDHF consistently improves multiple baselines across different DETR variants and achieves state-of-the-art performance on the evaluated benchmarks. The best ReDHF variants surpass their baselines by +1.4 AP on AI-TOD-v2, +1.6 AP on VisDrone, and +1.5 AP on SODA-D, with especially notable gains on tiny and small objects.

analysis.problem_statement: DETR-based detectors discard high-resolution features to reduce computational cost, causing the loss of fine-grained details necessary for detecting tiny objects.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Loss of spatial resolution and fine-grained feature details in transformer-based detection architectures due to downsampling and computational constraints.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses a critical limitation in transformer-based object detection where high-resolution features, essential for tiny object detection, are typically discarded to manage computational overhead. By proposing a framework that selectively revives and enhances these features without incurring prohibitive costs, it enables more accurate detection of small instances in complex scenes.

key_metrics.primary_metric: Average Precision (AP) improvement on tiny object detection benchmarks
key_metrics.metric_value: +1.4 AP on AI-TOD-v2, +1.6 AP on VisDrone, +1.5 AP on SODA-D
key_metrics.baseline: Respective DETR variant baselines
key_metrics.improvement_percentage: Not explicitly quantified as a percentage in the summary, but represents a consistent absolute AP gain across benchmarks.

technical_breakdown.method: The framework constructs a semantically enhanced highest-resolution feature and injects its details into shallow features using Cross-Scale Deformable Fusion. It applies Ellipse-Guided Shallow Supervision to learn reliable priors and uses Full-Scale Query Interaction to allow decoder queries to access both low-level and high-level information.
technical_breakdown.architecture: ReDHF framework comprising three components: Cross-Scale Deformable Fusion (CSDF), Ellipse-Guided Shallow Supervision (EGSS), and Full-Scale Query Interaction (FSQI).
technical_breakdown.implementation_details: CSDF uses deformable fusion to inject fine-grained details into shallow features at moderate cost. EGSS applies geometry-adaptive auxiliary supervision. FSQI enables decoder queries to aggregate cues from multiple scales.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Designed to operate under 'moderate cost' by selectively reviving high-resolution features rather than processing them fully, balancing computational efficiency with detection accuracy.

paper.title: Invariance before structure: two modes of emergent compression in representation learning
paper.summary: Learned representations show striking invariance across biological and artificial neural networks, with different substrates and variations driven by drift, heterogeneity and initialisation. To understand this invariance, we propose Emergent Adaptive Representation Learning (EARL), a framework that distinguishes two modes of emergence in learned representations: state-space compression, where a learned representation gains predictive power over its own future beyond what the network's units can predict individually, and parameter-space compression, where networks with different micro-level parameters converge to the same representation. We formalise both as Fisher sensitivities and introduce ensemble-level information-theoretic measures for each. In a recurrent reservoir with a trained bottleneck, parameter-space compression rises within the first few epochs of training and partly independently of the task, whereas state-space compression rises about 30 epochs later and only when the network begins to learn the temporal structure of the task. These results suggest that invariance to the substrate and task-specific emergent structure are acquired in distinct phases of learning.

paper.title: PVDepth: Panoramic Video Depth Estimation via Geometry-Aware Spatiotemporal Adaptation
paper.summary: Panoramic video depth estimation is pivotal for applications such as Virtual Reality and World Models. However, advancements in this field are impeded by two primary obstacles: the scarcity of large-scale training data and the unique spatiotemporal challenges of Equirectangular Projection (ERP), which hinder the direct transfer of perspective models. In this paper, we first present PanoCARLA, a large-scale synthetic RGB-D panoramic video dataset, featuring natural motion trajectories and drone-like roaming perspectives. Building on this foundation, we propose PVDepth, an end-to-end framework adapted from perspective video depth models. To tackle ERP-specific geometric distortions and consequent non-linear temporal dynamics, we introduce two core mechanisms: (1) A Progressive Sphere-aware Noise Initialization strategy that anneals the noise distribution from planar to spherical, guiding the model to adapt to non-uniform information density; and (2) A Cube-rectified Temporal Modeling module that incorporates an auxiliary cubemap temporal branch to rectify non-linear temporal dynamics in the ERP domain. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PVDepth achieves superior performance, generating geometrically accurate and temporally consistent depth sequences. Code and data will be released at https:// github.com/ChuanxinSong/PVDepth.

paper.title: Adapters as Data: The Latent Space of LoRAs
paper.summary: LoRA adapters are usually treated as finished artifacts rather than as a data modality. Prior work has shown that LoRA adapters populate a low-dimensional manifold that a linear PCA basis already organizes well enough to support different operations such as sampling, editing, and inversion. We ask what a learned, nonlinear latent adds beyond this. We train a transformer autoencoder on the same population of LoRA identity adapters, mapping each into a latent space and compare every operation against the identical operation applied directly to the raw adapter weights. The latent preserves the capabilities already available in weight space, sampling diverse identities and editing individual attributes. Beyond preservation, we show that the latent is far more robust to displacement than weight space, degrading into distorted but still valid faces rather than texture. Fixed-dimensional weight-space representations cannot natively host adapters of more than one rank, so we extend our sequential autoencoder to hold mixed-rank adapters within one shared latent. This gives a path toward treating adapter weights of varying architecture as a single, general modality rather than one tied to a fixed rank, and points to a learned, nonlinear latent as the mechanism that could carry this generalization further, toward heterogeneous populations of adapters.

paper.title: Seeing Beyond the Next Step: World-Model-Guided Human-Like Navigation in Multi-Agent Scenes
paper.summary: Selecting a next motion in a populated scene is not just a matter of avoiding what is currently in the way: an action can be locally feasible yet drift onto the road instead of the crosswalk, cut into a stream of crossing pedestrians, or bottleneck a narrow passage. These failure modes are invisible from the current state alone, and acting on them requires reasoning about what each candidate action will cause. World models offer exactly this, namely action-conditioned predictions of the future, but rolling them out at every decision step is a cost deployable navigation systems cannot pay, and the field has largely traded foresight for speed. We argue this is a false dichotomy. The natural place for a world model in human-aware navigation is at training time, as a preference oracle that distills foresight into a fast policy, rather than at inference time, as an online planner. We pair a discrete visual action prior with two task-aligned world models, one for nearby social dynamics and one for future scene semantics, that score candidate actions by their predicted consequences and refine the policy through group-relative preference distillation. At deployment, both world models are removed and the policy acts in a single forward pass. Across five held-out evaluation scenarios, this yields navigation that is simultaneously safer, more socially and group-coherent, and more goal-directed than strong reactive and learned baselines, with naive observers rating the resulting motion as more human-like. Taken together, our findings point to a different approach for bringing world-model foresight into deployable agents: not accelerating rollouts, but amortizing them into the policy so that the cost of looking ahead is confined to training. paper.title: Static Recovery Is Not Dynamic Stability: Dynamics-Aware Benchmarking of Protein Motif Scaffolding
paper.summary: Protein motif scaffolding benchmarks assess whether generative models can build scaffolds around functionally important residues. Their conclusions depend on which motifs are tested and which criteria define success. Existing benchmarks typically use small hand-curated motif sets and static refolding criteria, but protein function often depends on conformational ensembles and transitions. Here, we address both benchmark scope and success criteria. We introduce BILBY-PRO, a systematically derived benchmark of structurally conserved functional motifs from PROSITE-linked experimental structures, comprising 220 cases from 174 PROSITE motif-pattern entries. Evaluating six recent scaffold-generation models reveals distinct patterns in target coverage and unique-solution yield: RFDiffusion and Proteina solve more targets, whereas ESM3 produces more unique successful scaffolds on the targets it solves. We further introduce BILBY-MD, a reference-based all-atom molecular dynamics evaluation framework. Applied to statically solved designs from the original MotifBench benchmark, it compares motif drift, scaffold drift, motif-contact preservation, and motif-dihedral free-energy landscapes against reference simulations. Of 55 statically solved model-problem pairs, 31 satisfy our MD-supported criterion and only 8 pass all checks. Compact, self-contained motifs are often MD-supported, whereas interface-like or context-dependent motifs fail more frequently. Static refolding success therefore provides useful evidence of local motif recovery but does not establish dynamical fidelity of the full scaffold. BILBY highlights three complementary axes of motif-scaffolding evaluation: target coverage, unique-solution yield, and MD-supported dynamical fidelity.

paper.title: AffineGS: Unlocking Accurate Geometry in 3DGS via Spatially Varying Affine Rectification
paper.summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has become the leading approach for photorealistic novel view synthesis, yet its geometric accuracy lags behind its visual quality. Existing depth-guided methods attempt to resolve this by regularizing the optimization with monocular depth priors, typically using a single global scale-and-shift alignment. Crucially, we discover a fundamental flaw in this assumption: modern monocular depth networks systematically exhibit region-dependent, piecewise-linear distortions. This discovery invalidates standard global alignment strategies, which warp scene geometry by enforcing a single transform. To address this, we introduce a spatially varying affine rectification model that corrects monocular disparity into consistent metric depth using regionally smooth, edge-aware fields. We further derive a normal-aware regularizer that uses spatial gradients to couple the rectified disparity with 3DGS depth and normals. Across diverse experimental settings, our sensor-free method shows strong photometric quality of Gaussian Splatting while substantially improving geometric accuracy and outperforming state-of-the art geometry-focused methods.

paper.title: FlyingDrones: A Dataset and Benchmark for Optical Flow Estimation from UAV motion
paper.summary: Optical flow is an important cue for drone analysis in aerial surveillance, airspace monitoring, and long-range target tracking, where motion remains informative when appearance is weak. Estimating the motion of small Unmanned Aerial Vehicles, however, is difficult because distant targets occupy few pixels, have low contrast, and move against complex dynamic backgrounds. Standard optical-flow benchmarks emphasize large, object-centric motions and therefore do not characterize distant aerial targets well. We introduce FlyingDrones, a generated benchmark with dense ground-truth optical flow and segmentation masks derived from physically based rendering, and define resolution-normalized metrics (EPE Norm) that normalize flow by image dimensions. We evaluate 16 state-of-the-art model families on a motion- and size-stratified subset of 999 flow pairs at three resolutions. Every family recovers drone motion better than the zero-flow reference, but the gap between families widens with resolution: at 1920x1080, global-matching, recurrent, transformer, and short-window temporal models separate clearly from pyramid, classical, self-supervised, lightweight, and diffusion models. Within-family checkpoint spread is comparable to or larger than between-family spread, so the training curriculum is as important as the architecture. Two complementary studies test the benchmark beyond synthetic accuracy: a ground-truth-free motion-alignment evaluation on 21 cameras of real UAV footage shows that the synthetic ranking carries a moderate, significant signal about real-world performance (Spearman \r{ho} = 0.63 over 41 checkpoints) while the exact top ranks differ, and a fine-tuning study shows that 800 FlyingDrones pairs reduce held-out drone-region error by up to 37% and improve drone localization on the real footage for all four architectures tested.

analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses a critical gap in computer vision by introducing FlyingDrones, a physically based rendering (PBR) dataset with dense ground-truth optical flow specifically designed for small UAV targets. It demonstrates that while all state-of-the-art models outperform zero-flow baselines, performance disparities widen significantly at higher resolutions, and that training curriculum impacts performance as much as architecture choice.

paper.title: Non-Parametric Mutual Information Estimation with Vine Copulas
paper.summary: We introduce VINE: a non-parametric mutual information (MI) estimator based on simplified D-vine copulas. We compare VINE against SotA neural MI estimators on a range of datasets, both under settings where the simplified D-vine assumption holds and where it is violated, demonstrating competitive accuracy at a lower computational cost for low- to medium-dimensional datasets.

paper.title: Calibrated Target Noise Recovers Curvature from the Gradients
paper.summary: Estimating curvature information from gradients alone is a fundamental problem in machine learning. The challenge becomes particularly acute in settings where only aggregate mini-batch gradients are available, yet curvature information is still required for applications such as preconditioning in optimisation, sampling, and early stopping. Perhaps surprisingly, we show that a simple target-perturbation scheme suffices to recover such curvature information from gradients alone. Our method injects zero-mean noise into the targets, with variance calibrated to the local output curvature. The covariance of the resulting noisy batch gradients then recovers practical curvature matrices, without requiring per-sample gradients, second-order derivatives, or other internal network quantities. For a broad class of non-linear models, our scheme recovers the Generalised Gauss--Newton (GGN) matrix; for feed-forward ReLU networks, it additionally recovers the diagonal blocks of the population Hessian. We demonstrate that the resulting estimator is simple, lightweight, provably optimal, and easy to integrate into existing training pipelines. Experiments demonstrate accurate curvature recovery, faster optimisation when the estimator is used for preconditioning, and the utility of the estimated GGN for early stopping.

analysis.executive_summary: This paper introduces a lightweight, zero-cost method to estimate curvature by injecting calibrated noise into training targets, enabling the use of second-order optimization benefits without the prohibitive cost of explicit Hessian computation. It bridges the gap between first-order gradient information and second-order curvature needs, making sophisticated optimization strategies accessible for standard training pipelines.

paper.title: Towards Real-Time Full-Waveform LiDAR Transformers via Intensity-Guided Token Reduction and Physics-Aware Augmentation
paper.summary: LiDAR is a critical sensor for autonomous driving and robotics, yet it remains vulnerable to adverse conditions such as fog, rain, transparent objects, and low-reflectance surfaces. Full-waveform LiDAR (FWL) addresses these limitations by capturing the complete return waveform as a histogram, preserving rich reflection characteristics including multi-path echoes and weak signals. While recent Transformer-based approaches have demonstrated promise on FWL data, two fundamental bottlenecks remain: high computational cost from redundant tokens in low-intensity background regions, and limited generalization due to scarce annotated training data. We address both bottlenecks by exploiting the physical structure inherent to FWL data. First, we propose FWL-ToPM, a token pruning and merging mechanism that leverages intensity distributions to selectively reduce tokens while retaining critical waveform content. Second, we introduce FWLAug, a data augmentation framework designed as a regularization method that preserves waveform structure, retaining the Time-of-Flight waveform of each ray and the frustum geometry, to improve generalization to unseen scenes. Evaluated on the Ghost-FWL benchmark, FWL-ToPM achieves over 8 times speedup at real-time throughput alongside a nearly 9-point F1 gain over the prior state of the art, establishing the first real-time FWL Transformer that simultaneously improves accuracy. FWLAug further improves performance on both the standard benchmark and an out-of-distribution test set of unseen scenes. Together, these methods push FWL-based perception toward practical deployment. The code and the OOD dataset are publicly available and can be accessed via the project page: https://keio-csg.github.io/FWL-ToPM

analysis.executive_summary: This work enables the practical deployment of Full-Waveform LiDAR by resolving the trade-off between the rich information content of waveform data and the computational constraints of real-time systems. By introducing physics-aware token reduction and augmentation, it achieves real-time throughput with improved accuracy, bridging the gap between high-fidelity sensing and operational viability in robotics.

paper.title: Align Before Aggregation: Basis-Consistent Federated LoRA under Heterogeneous Ranks
paper.summary: Federated fine-tuning of large language models (LLMs) under heterogeneous client capacities is increasingly important, and low-rank adaptation (LoRA) with heterogeneous ranks makes it practical. Existing server-side aggregators compose local matrix updates $ΔW_i$ from client-specific LoRA factors $(A_i,B_i)$ before aggregating them. Although these matrix updates lie in the same weight space $\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}$ and can be averaged directly, the LoRA factors that generate them may expressed client-specific local basis. In the typical compose--aggregate--factorize--dispatch loop, this basis inconsistency can make the rank-$r_i$ reference prefix dispatched to lower-rank clients unstable after server-side refactorization. In this work, we propose \textbf{FedAbA}, a basis-consistent federated LoRA aggregation framework for heterogeneous ranks. FedAbA first extracts each client's local basis, aligns it to the corresponding prefix of the global reference basis, and constructs a basis-consistent reconstruction of each local matrix update before aggregation. It then aggregates these reconstructions with weights that combine client data size and consistency score, followed by exact coefficient-space SVD refactorization and gauge fixing before rank-prefix dispatch. Our theoretical analysis clarifies the role of basis consistency and supports the proposed consistency-aware aggregation mechanism. Extensive experiments show that FedAbA outperforms representative federated LoRA baselines, with the largest gains under the strongest rank heterogeneity.

analysis.executive_summary: This work solves a critical structural issue in federated LLM fine-tuning where heterogeneous client capacities lead to inconsistent basis representations, causing instability in server-side aggregation and dispatch. By enforcing basis consistency before aggregation, the method enables stable and effective collaboration among clients with varying computational resources, which is essential for scalable, real-world federated learning deployments.

paper.title: TACT-KV: Tri-Axis Cosine Transform for Compressing Volumetric KV Caches in Medical VLMs
paper.summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) applied to 3D medical scans face a structural memory wall. A single CT or MRI volume produces tens of thousands of vision tokens, and the resulting key-value (KV) cache scales linearly with both batch and context. Existing KV compression methods operate on the cache's feature or token statistics, or apply 1D and 2D transforms, leaving the three-axis spatial structure in the cache unexploited. We propose TACT-KV (Tri-Axis Cosine Transform), a calibration-free KV compression method that exploits strong spatial correlations in visual KV states along all three anatomical axes of 3D scans. This correlation concentrates the KV cache energy under a frequency-domain transform. TACT-KV applies a separable 3D discrete cosine transform to the KV cache, allocates a per-layer bit budget across frequency bins via reverse water-filling (more bits to high-energy components), and quantizes each bin with a fixed scalar codebook. We derive a close-form relation: the distortion reduction from adaptive bit allocation is dominated by the spectral concentration of the transformed cache. Across six medical VLMs and two 3D CT benchmarks, TACT-KV achieves the lowest 1-bit prediction-flip rate on eleven of twelve model and dataset pairs in our main comparison. The same advantage reproduces on four general-purpose VLMs evaluated on video tasks, indicating that the benefit of exploiting three-axis structure generalizes beyond medical imaging. At equal high-bandwidth memory (HBM), TACT-KV scales the decoding batch size on a single GPU by up to $8\times$.

analysis.problem_statement: Vision-language models applied to 3D medical scans suffer from a structural memory wall due to the linear scaling of key-value (KV) caches with batch size and context length, which existing compression methods fail to address by ignoring the three-axis spatial structure of the data.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Memory bandwidth and capacity constraints (HBM) during the decoding phase of large-scale vision-language models processing volumetric data.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the critical memory bottleneck in deploying VLMs for 3D medical imaging by exploiting spatial correlations in KV caches. By applying a 3D discrete cosine transform, it enables significant compression without calibration, allowing for up to 8x larger batch sizes on a single GPU. This is crucial for scaling medical AI applications where high-resolution volumetric data generates massive token counts.

technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Uses a close-form relation to determine bit allocation via reverse water-filling; employs a fixed scalar codebook for quantization; exploits tri-axis spatial correlations in anatomical structures.
technical_breakdown.code_complexity: Calibration-free (no training required); computational overhead is dominated by the 3D DCT and inverse transform, but the reduction in HBM usage allows for significantly larger batch sizes, improving overall throughput.

paper.title: Fine-Tuning a Transducer for Impaired Speech: Where the Gains Appear and What They Mean for Evaluation
paper.summary: Speech recognition still works poorly for many people whose speech is affected by conditions such as ALS, Parkinson's disease, cerebral palsy, Down syndrome or stroke. We took part in the Speech Accessibility Project Challenge 2 (SAPC2) with a public speech recognizer that we fine-tuned on the challenge data. Our best entry scored 7.81% character error rate on Test1, the first of two hidden test sets (official baseline 15.26%). Our live entries ran on CPUs with a combined median latency of about 0.9 seconds at 7.96-8.07% error. On new speakers, fine-tuning reduced errors most for the speakers that an off-the-shelf recognizer finds hardest to understand. Sentences already seen in training had far lower error rates than new ones (2.58% vs 6.42%), a larger difference than being a familiar speaker made. We close with lessons for evaluating such systems.

paper.title: Stress Testing Chain-of-Thought Monitoring Against Covert Misalignment
paper.summary: As LLM agents advance rapidly in autonomy, the risk of hidden objectives that bypass safety constraints becomes increasingly plausible. Chain-of-thought (CoT) monitoring offers a key control mechanism by reading the agent's reasoning and flagging misalignment before it materializes into action, yet its reliability depends on the realism of the red-team it is stress-tested against. Existing red-teaming efforts rely on shared templates, such as casting a side task as a prerequisite, which treat the side objective as an exogenous insertion and leave task-specific, contextually grounded evasions underexplored. We therefore ask: How robust is CoT monitoring against agents that strategically conceal misalignment? To answer this, we introduce TraceMRT, an automated Trace-level Monitor Red-Teaming framework that reframes the side task as a coherent sub-goal of the primary task and searches trace-shaping strategies whose induced trajectories complete the misaligned objective while reading as natural execution. Through black-box attacks on state-of-the-art monitors such as GPT-5.2 and Claude-4.5, we reveal substantial vulnerabilities even in top models. To counter these vulnerabilities, we propose a Bayesian Trajectory Monitoring framework, integrating global context and local segment evidence to detect covert misalignment. Empirically, our method significantly consolidates monitor robustness with 0.91 AUC and 0.74 TPR@FPR=0.05.

This work demonstrates that state-of-the-art monitors (like GPT-5.2 and Claude-4.5) are vulnerable to contextually grounded, trace-shaping attacks that make misaligned behavior appear as natural execution. It proposes a Bayesian monitoring framework to significantly improve detection robustness against these covert evasions.

paper.title: Georeferenced Cross-View 3D Reconstruction from Ground and Satellite Images
paper.summary: Georeferenced 3D reconstruction from ground images requires recovering not only the local scene geometry, but also localizing every camera center and 3D point in a geographic coordinate frame. Existing cross-view geo-localization methods are able to estimate the GPS coordinate of a single ground camera, but do not reconstruct dense 3D geometry, while recent feed-forward multi-view 3D reconstruction models predict point maps and camera poses only in a local coordinate frame. We introduce X-VGGT, a feed-forward cross-view geometry transformer that unifies these tasks by jointly processing a set of ground-level images and a georeferenced satellite image to predict ground-view camera poses, dense 3D point maps, and a scene-level transform parameterized by gravity, scale, yaw and translation. This transform projects the local reconstruction into the satellite plane, resulting in the geo-registration of all ground images with the georeferenced satellite image. We further propose an evaluation protocol for this joint task and show that, across multiple cross-view datasets, X-VGGT produces accurate georeferenced reconstructions and outperforms prior cross-view geo-localization and multi-view 3D reconstruction models.

analysis.bottleneck_addressed: The lack of unified feed-forward models that can simultaneously perform dense multi-view 3D reconstruction and cross-view geo-localization, which are typically treated as separate tasks with different coordinate frame constraints.
analysis.executive_summary: This work bridges the gap between local 3D reconstruction and global geo-localization by introducing a unified transformer architecture that processes heterogeneous ground and satellite inputs. It enables the direct projection of local 3D reconstructions into a geographic frame, which is critical for applications like autonomous navigation, digital twins, and large-scale mapping where precise global alignment is required.

paper.title: SKIM: Pruning Large Language Model Agents via Selective Knowledge Informed Masking
paper.summary: Large Language Model (LLM) agents are increasingly deployed under structured generation, where grammar constraints enforce output format at inference time. Whereas existing compression methods target unconstrained generation, we first identify a fundamental mismatch: under structured generation, grammar constraints reduce the model's output distribution to valid tokens, and the logits matter most at the small set of positions that decide the agent's action. Motivated by this finding, we propose SKIM (Selective Knowledge-Informed Masking), the first pruning and distillation framework for LLM agents under structured generation, with both stages guided by token role. SKIM partitions token positions into context, decision, and format categories, and this partition drives two complementary axes: (1) category-aware pruning saliency scores that preserve parameters most relevant for decision positions; and (2) an on-policy distillation objective that aligns student and teacher on valid tokens, paired with category-aware feature matching. We evaluate SKIM on tool-calling benchmarks and within multi-step agent loops, across multiple model scales and sparsity levels. SKIM consistently improves accuracy over baselines, with its superiority becoming most striking in high-sparsity regimes where conventional methods struggle, demonstrating the potential of category-aware compression for deployment-time grammar-constrained agents.

analysis.problem_statement: Existing LLM compression methods fail to account for the specific token role distributions in structured generation, leading to suboptimal pruning and distillation for grammar-constrained agents.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Inference efficiency and model compression for structured/grammar-constrained generation tasks.
analysis.executive_summary: SKIM addresses the mismatch between general-purpose compression techniques and the specific requirements of structured generation, where only a small set of 'decision' tokens significantly impacts agent actions. By introducing category-aware pruning and distillation, it enables more aggressive sparsity without the accuracy degradation typically seen in conventional methods, facilitating the deployment of efficient LLM agents.

key_metrics.baseline: Conventional pruning and distillation methods for unconstrained generation

technical_breakdown.method: SKIM partitions token positions into context, decision, and format categories to guide both pruning saliency scores and on-policy distillation objectives.

paper.title: Semantics-to-Contact: A Stagewise Framework for Robust Contact-Rich Manipulation
paper.summary: Contact-rich manipulation requires precise control under complex contact dynamics while remaining robust to diverse visual conditions. However, real-world reinforcement learning often overfits to the visual appearance of training scenes. We propose Semantics-to-Contact (S2C), a stagewise framework for visually robust contact-rich manipulation. The insight is to decompose the problem into two stages: semantic focusing and contact refinement. In the first stage, a vision-language model localizes task-relevant regions across visually diverse scenes, providing coarse spatial guidance and reducing the burden of exploration. In the second stage, a real-world human-in-the-loop residual reinforcement learning policy learns fine-grained contact behaviors within the localized region using force feedback. To further improve visual robustness, we introduce an object-centric visual augmentation strategy that randomizes background appearance while preserving the robot and task-relevant objects. Experiments on six contact-rich real-world manipulation tasks exhibit that S2C consistently improves success rates over strong baselines and maintains reliable performance under significant visual and positional variations. These results demonstrate that stagewise semantic focusing and contact refinement provide a practical path toward visually robust real-world contact-rich manipulation. Our demos can be seen in https://edem-ai.github.io/S2C/.

analysis.problem_statement: Real-world reinforcement learning for contact-rich manipulation often overfits to specific visual appearances, leading to poor robustness under diverse visual and positional conditions.
analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Visual robustness and generalization in real-world reinforcement learning for manipulation tasks.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the critical challenge of deploying manipulation policies in uncontrolled real-world environments where visual conditions vary significantly. By decoupling semantic localization from fine-grained contact control, it offers a practical framework that reduces exploration burden and enhances policy stability. This is significant for the current AI landscape as it moves robotics beyond simulation-to-reality gaps by leveraging vision-language models for robust spatial grounding.

key_metrics.baseline: Strong baselines (unspecified in summary)

technical_breakdown.method: A stagewise framework that first uses a vision-language model to localize task-relevant regions for coarse guidance, followed by a human-in-the-loop residual reinforcement learning policy to learn fine-grained contact behaviors using force feedback.
technical_breakdown.architecture: Two-stage pipeline: 1) VLM-based semantic focusing module, 2) Residual RL policy with force feedback integration, supported by an object-centric visual augmentation strategy.

paper.title: JailBound: FOL-Guided Jailbreak Evaluation for Exploring LLM Behavioral Boundaries
paper.summary: As large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as general-purpose conversational assistants, they must handle diverse user requests while reliably refusing harmful ones. Jailbreak attacks craft adversarial instructions or conversational contexts to elicit unsafe responses despite these safeguards. However, existing jailbreak benchmarks often rely on manually designed or collected prompts, making it difficult to systematically extend coverage to new threat conditions. Moreover, existing attack search methods typically optimize for attack success rate (ASR), providing limited insight into how model behavior changes locally between safe refusal and unsafe response. To address these limitations, we present JailBound, a unified jailbreak evaluation framework that combines automated benchmark construction with first-order loss (FOL)-guided dual-branch search. JailBound organizes threats by risk category, application domain, and attack type. Conditioned on this taxonomy, a fine-tuned meta-attack generator synthesizes evaluation prompts across diverse threat conditions. FOL serves as a local sensitivity signal for exploring high-value attack states and behavior-sensitive states. We evaluate JailBound across 46 LLMs from 13 model families under a unified experimental protocol. Under matched settings, the High-Value Branch improves average ASR over a ZOL-only baseline by 5.1 and 4.9 percentage points across the two evaluation settings. Under local perturbations, states from the Safety-Sensitivity Branch exhibit higher behavioral flip rates than those from the High-Value Branch across all tested radii for JailBound and S-Eval, indicating greater local sensitivity of judge-assigned safety labels. paper.title: Echoes of Error: Residual-Directional Local Rollout Consistency for Timeseries Forecasting
paper.summary: In time-series forecasting, rollout errors are not merely one-step fitting discrepancies: once fed back into the evolving state, they can perturb future predictions. We formalize this effect through local rollout consistency, which compares the next prediction produced under teacher forcing with that produced under free running. In principle, this consistency can be enforced directly by tracking the residual-induced perturbation of the next state. In practice, however, the residual-to-state alignment operator is often difficult to design when the input state and output block have different dimensions, heterogeneous components, or architecture-dependent layouts. We therefore use a first-order local surrogate that penalizes the Jacobian-vector product of the predictor along the actual feedback perturbation, suppressing precisely the directions through which self-generated errors remain visible to future predictions. We further give the same loss a geometric interpretation near a predictive manifold: by controlling residual-induced directions that probe the normal bundle, the objective yields theoretical conditions under which free-running trajectories remain inside a stability tube around the manifold. Experiments on time series forecasting tasks support this view, showing that the proposed regularization improves predictive accuracy. More broadly, our results suggest a training principle for time-series forecasters and sequential predictors: a model should not only make small one-step errors, but also learn not to let its own errors echo into the future. Code is available at https://github.com/Wangzzzzzzzz/Echoes-Of-Error.

analysis.executive_summary: This work introduces a training regularization technique that aligns the model's behavior under teacher forcing with its behavior under free-running, thereby suppressing error directions that propagate into future states. By ensuring local rollout consistency, the method enhances the robustness of time-series forecasters against self-generated errors, offering a principled approach to improving long-horizon prediction stability.

paper.title: When Scores Conflict with Preferences: Pre-Alignment Diagnosis and Adaptive Correction of Constraint Drift in DPO
paper.summary: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO) is increasingly used in settings where pairwise preferences coexist with pointwise criteria such as response length, answer correctness, or safety scores. When the two disagree, standard DPO treats pairs whose preferred output scores worse on the pointwise criterion (conflict pairs) in the same way as the remaining (matching) pairs. We characterize a systematic failure mode, constraint drift: for sufficiently small updates, conflict pairs tend to increase constraint cost while matching pairs tend to repair it, and the net change depends on their balance. This balance yields a closed-form pre-alignment diagnostic, $ρ^{*}_{\mathrm{eq}}$, computable from dataset statistics, that indicates whether a dataset is self-correcting or requires intervention. Building on this diagnostic, we propose Conflict-aware DPO (CoDPO), which down-weights conflict pairs with a strength set from $ρ^{*}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ rather than tuned, and adds an adaptive margin shift that addresses residual drift during training. Empirically, drift grows monotonically with conflict exposure on the conflict-dominated domains, and the intervention decision given by $ρ^{*}_{\mathrm{eq}}$ matches the observed drift on every domain, including one that it identifies as self-correcting. On all four domains of the main comparison, CoDPO reduces drift while largely preserving the preference learning of vanilla DPO. Compared with hard filtering and recent constrained and multi-objective baselines, CoDPO also achieves a more favorable drift-preference trade-off.

analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses a critical reliability gap in LLM alignment where standard DPO inadvertently worsens safety or format constraints when preference data conflicts with pointwise scores. By introducing a closed-form diagnostic to identify self-correcting datasets and a new CoDPO method that adaptively down-weights conflicting pairs, it enables more robust alignment that preserves preference learning without sacrificing constraint adherence.

paper.title: Permanent and Transient Representations for Continual Reinforcement Learning
paper.summary: Continual Reinforcement Learning (CRL) agents struggle to adapt to new situations while retaining prior knowledge, leading to a stability-plasticity trade-off. One approach to solving this problem is by using complementary learning systems: one for slow, long-term learning and another for quick, transient adaptation. Anand & Precup (2023) instantiated this idea using permanent and transient value functions, but used the same features in both systems. Intuitively, long-term learning should rely more on parametric representations for broad generalization, while transient learning would be best served by non-parametric representations for situation-specific adaptation. In this paper, we explore this idea both theoretically and empirically. By introducing a novel non-parametric approximation for estimating the transient value function in complex tasks, we demonstrate that our method enables online learning and outperforms competitive baselines on image-based tasks and Craftax-Classic, underscoring the effectiveness of our system-level decomposition.

analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Catastrophic forgetting and the lack of effective mechanisms for simultaneous long-term generalization and short-term situational adaptation in non-stationary environments.
analysis.executive_summary: This work resolves the limitation of previous complementary learning systems that relied on identical features for both permanent and transient learning. By decoupling the representations—using parametric models for long-term stability and non-parametric approximations for transient plasticity—it enables more robust online learning. This is significant for developing AI agents that can operate effectively in complex, evolving environments like image-based tasks and open-world simulations.

paper.title: Householder Motion Embedding: Noise Modulation for Motion-Controllable Video Generation
paper.summary: Diffusion models for video generation have achieved remarkable success, yet precise motion control under explicit user guidance remains challenging. Recent noise-warping methods introduce temporal correlations by warping the noise according to the user-provided motion signal. However, standard spatial warping generally disrupts the noise's i.i.d. Gaussian structure, requiring distribution correction, such as Jacobian-based correction, but at a substantial computational overhead. We propose Householder Motion Embedding (HME), which encodes the motion signal into the noise through a sequence of Householder reflections that together form an orthogonal transformation applied to each location's channel vector. HME exactly preserves the spatial Gaussian structure within each frame while introducing cross-frame correlations that promote temporally consistent video. HME is agnostic to the network architecture and integrates directly into standard video diffusion fine-tuning pipelines. Experiments on different scenarios show that HME matches or outperforms the state of the art, while achieving a 2.7x speedup over noise warping. These results demonstrate that channel-space Householder transformations offer a principled and efficient alternative to noise warping for motion-controllable video generation.

analysis.bottleneck_addressed: Computational inefficiency and distributional distortion in motion-controllable video generation pipelines.
analysis.executive_summary: This paper addresses the trade-off between motion controllability and computational efficiency in video diffusion models. By using Householder reflections to encode motion signals into the noise channel space, it preserves the Gaussian distribution exactly while introducing necessary temporal correlations. This allows for efficient integration into standard fine-tuning pipelines without the heavy cost of Jacobian-based corrections.

key_metrics.baseline: Standard noise warping methods with distribution correction

technical_breakdown.implementation_details: Uses orthogonal transformations (Householder reflections) to introduce cross-frame correlations while exactly preserving the spatial Gaussian structure within each frame, eliminating the need for Jacobian-based distribution correction.

paper.title: Scenario Augmentation for Rare Financial Events via Multimodal Latent Diffusion
paper.summary: Extreme market movements are scarce, heterogeneous, and difficult to learn from imbalanced historical data. We study whether generative augmentation can improve the representation and classification of CVaR-labeled rare financial windows while retaining the complementary structure exposed by different financial representations. Each market window is expressed through three aligned modalities: structured market variables, a spatial image transformation, and a sequence of portfolio returns. Separate variational autoencoders map the modalities to compact latent codes, and a class-conditional diffusion model learns their joint latent distribution. Conditional Value-at-Risk (CVaR) provides a risk-aware definition of rare windows and directs generation toward the minority regime. Across four window lengths on U.S. technology equities, the resulting synthetic samples improve fidelity and support relative to tabular diffusion baselines. An XGBoost classifier trained with real and generated samples attains AUCs of 0.953 - 0.960, exceeding both tabular generators and the corresponding real-only baselines. These results show that multimodal latent generation can provide useful synthetic stress scenarios for data-scarce financial risk models.

analysis.executive_summary: This work demonstrates that multimodal latent diffusion can generate high-fidelity synthetic stress scenarios that improve risk classification performance beyond tabular baselines. It is significant for the AI landscape as it provides a robust framework for augmenting scarce, heterogeneous financial data while preserving complex structural relationships across different data modalities.

paper.title: Efficient Diffusion Policy Fine Tuning with Latent Noise Representation Bridging
paper.summary: Pre-trained diffusion and flow policies have emerged as powerful backbones for robotics, yet adapting them to novel data via reinforcement learning (RL) remains computationally expensive, sample inefficient and lacks theoretical guarantees. Prior approaches that fine-tune the initial noise bypass costly backpropagation through time but struggle with the "noise aliasing" problem: there does not exista natural link between the noise space value and the action space value. This paper resolves these challenges by introducing the Latent Noise Linear Markov Decision Process (LNL-MDP). We derive the Bridge Equation for LNL-MDPs which eliminates the noise aliasing problem by aligning values with a shared representation between the noise and the action space. Furthermore, our LNL-MDP fine tuning framework falls under the FineTuneRL theory with near-optimal guarantee. Leveraging these insights, we propose Latent Representation Bridging for Diffusion (LARBRID), an algorithm that efficiently learns the representation to optimize the initial distribution that steers the pre-trained model to act optimally in the environment. It yields up to 2-3$\times$ performance increases on challenging control problems across a diverse suite of robotic locomotion and manipulation tasks. Code can be found at: github.com/Maincode-Research/LARBRID.git.

paper.title: FRESHPart: Feedback-Reshaped Spectral Embedding for Hypergraph Partitioning
paper.summary: With scalable Laplacian solvers now available, the next frontier is to exploit them more effectively for high-quality hypergraph partitioning. In this work, we revisit spectral hypergraph partitioning from the perspective of spectral embedding geometry. Through a systematic analysis of circuit hypergraphs and controlled synthetic (hyper)graphs, we identify a ray-like embedding structure that helps explain the effectiveness of projection-based partitioning. We further show that the geometry of spectral embeddings can be systematically influenced through Laplacian design and hyperedge reweighting. Guided by these insights, we propose FRESHPart, a feedback-reshaped spectral partitioning framework that refines the spectral embedding through Geometry Feedback and Search Feedback, producing embeddings that are better aligned with projection-based partitioning. On the Titan23 benchmark, FRESHPart achieves average cut reductions over hMETIS of 13.09% at $ε=2\%$ and 25.21% at $ε=20\%$, surpassing the strongest previously reported results (12.16% and 22.53%, respectively), while completing every benchmark in under 120 s on a single GPU.

analysis.executive_summary: This paper advances the state-of-the-art in hypergraph partitioning, a critical step in VLSI design automation, by introducing a feedback-reshaped spectral embedding method. By systematically analyzing embedding geometry, it achieves significant cut reductions over standard tools like hMETIS while maintaining high computational efficiency on a single GPU.
